Built the Customers page at the app root:

- **`services/customers.contract.ts`** — `Customer` shape and a `CustomerApi` interface (`list(signal)`).
- **`services/customers.http.ts`** — the live adapter, `fetch('/api/customers')`, throwing an `Error` with the server's message on non-2xx or network failure.
- **`services/customers.context.ts`** — DI plumbing, same pattern as `devices.context.ts`.
- **`modules/customers/`** — `customers.queries.ts` (`useCustomers`, a `useQuery` with retry/backoff), `Customers.tsx` (loading/error/table states, `data-testid="loading"|"error"|"retry"|"customer-row"`, exactly one visible at a time via early returns), `index.ts`, `customers.css`.
- **`main.tsx`** — now mounts `<Customers>` with the HTTP adapter instead of the devices demo.
- **`styles/global.css`** — registered `customers.css`.

Verified against the live server (`http://127.0.0.1:55180`) by mounting the real `useCustomers` hook in happy-dom: it starts pending, then resolves with all 25 customers fetched from `GET /api/customers`. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` both exit 0. The pre-existing `devices`/`reading` modules were left untouched, just no longer mounted.

Done. The fix was in `modules/customers/customers.queries.ts`: `useCustomers` had `retry: 2` with backoff (copied from the devices module), so a single refused load was silently retried twice by TanStack Query before ever surfacing as an error, and clicking Retry on top of that fired even more requests. I set `retry: false`, so now:

- a refused load reports the error after exactly one attempt — no hidden retries, no rows, no loader
- the Retry button's `refetch()` is the only thing that ever asks again, and it asks exactly once
- `isPending`/`isError`/`isSuccess` stay mutually exclusive throughout, which the component's early-return structure turns directly into "never two of loader/error/table visible at once"

Verified against a fake API that fails once then succeeds (call-counted), and `pnpm lint` / `pnpm typecheck` both exit 0.
